text:
sara: Quick follow-up from the thin-queue-proxy spike. Goal was to offload eviction churn from the continuous batcher and see if pre-admission helps tail latency.

sara: High-level behaviour: proxy accepts requests for a small admission window (3-7ms), annotates cost_hint, runs a cheap eviction pass, then forwards. If proxy is unhealthy gateway bypasses it.

matt: Nice. What did the admission pass do exactly? simple LRU?

sara: We tested three lightweight policies: LRU, cost-aware-LRU (cost per token), and tenant-soft-quota (tokens with soft limits). Default run used cost-aware-LRU.

leo: Any numbers? we care about end-to-end latencies and restart counts.

sara: Short A/B (1h):
- baseline: p50 20ms, p95 130ms, p99 250ms, eviction-restarts 480/h
- proxy: p50 23ms, p95 115ms, p99 170ms, eviction-restarts 280/h
Throughput ~ flat. CPU on batcher down ~8%.

matt: Big p99 win. But p50 regressed slightly. Is the proxy added hop the cause?

sara: Yes small fixed hop + serialization cost. But proxy reduced large batch restarts that caused long tail.

nina: Concern: fairness. cost-aware-LRU can starve large single-tenant workloads that are latency-insensitive but throughput-critical.

sara: We saw that pattern. To mitigate we experimented with tenant_soft_quota and a periodic replenishment lofting for bursty tenants. Config snippet: 
`admission_window_ms=5; eviction_policy=cost_aware_lru; tenant_soft_quota=12k_tokens; quota_refill_interval_ms=1000`

leo: How does proxy track tokens without exploding memory? per-tenant maps are scary.

sara: Implementation uses a compact atomic sketch per-proxy for hot tenants and an LRU-bounded tenant table. Default fallback is stateless: rely solely on per-request cost_hint from gateway. Only enable per-tenant tables for Dedicated clusters.

matt: Ordering constraints? customers using streaming or multi-call sequences might depend on ordering.

sara: We added `x-ordering=seq` header. Proxy will not reorder or evict requests marked with that header. We also keep reordering window <= admission_window to limit out-of-order impact.

nina: Observability to add: why_evicted, tenant_token_estimate, admission_latency_ms, forwarded_window_size. Also correlate with batcher.eviction_origin.

sara: Agreed. I've logged these in the experiment trace. ci-bot pushed artifacts: `ci-bot: artifacts uploaded s3://ci-artifacts/thin-queue/6182741111/`

leo: Deployment model? sidecar vs shared service tradeoffs?

sara: Sidecar wins for locality and stable latency in spike tests. Shared service simplified memory but introduced inter-node network jitter in p50. Sidecar also simpler fail-open logic.

matt: Failure modes: if proxy OOMs or GC pauses we'll route to bypass. Need circuit-breaker in gateway.

sara: Plan: gateway healthcheck + fast bypass flag; sidecar will also expose `x-proxy-uptime` metrics.

nina: What about security and SDK changes? opt-out header for reordering, and flag to opt into proxy hints. Matt can add to SDK.

matt: I'll add `x-ordering=seq` and `x-proxy-hint: cost=...` to SDKs. Also include sample code.

leo: Next engineering tasks: memory hardening (approx counters, bounded tables), fairness knobs (quota refill), ramp playbook (telemetry thresholds). I'll prototype a fairness simulator.

sara: Owners: nina=telemetry/dashboards, matt=sdk headers/docs, leo=sidecar memory + sim, sara=rollout playbook.

nina: I'll add dashboards including per-tenant p99 delta and proxy.evictions.by_reason.

matt: One more operational note: add metric to detect proxy-induced stalls: `proxy.admit_latency_ms.buckets` and an alert when p95 > 10ms above baseline.

sara: Good. TL;DR: proxy adds ~2-4ms p50, reduces eviction restarts and p99 significantly in prelims. Requires fairness tuning, telemetry, SDK headers, and a well-tested bypass. Plan to iterate behind feature flag for dedicated customers first. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: deploy: thin-queue-proxy v0.2 -> green (rollout gated)
